comment: SECOND-CORPUS probe set: orc-sim-b (project 79a0c777-cad0-41ad-b639-5460b732000e, /home/yanneck/Work/orc-sim-b). Same schema and same `category` vocabulary as probes.json, different note ids — probes.json names orc-sim's ids and grades every positive as a miss here. Run: `bun /home/yanneck/Work/orchestrator/bench/graph-bench.ts /home/yanneck/Work/orchestrator/bench/probes-orc-sim-b.json` FROM /home/yanneck/Work/orc-sim-b (loadConfig resolves the project from cwd). Corpus shape is the point: 8 searchable semantic notes, ALL about the embedding subsystem, so every note is semantically adjacent to every other — the hard case for a cosine floor. Queries are phrased as a reader who does not know the note's title would ask; title words are NOT lifted into queries, because the keyword arm matches on terms and a title-copied query manufactures the very result being tested. The 7 negatives are copied VERBATIM from probes.json (kubernetes/graphql/stripe/kafka/android are absent from both corpora, so they port directly).

search.why: names the algorithm by its technical name; body of area-embedding-clustering is the only place either word appears ('Average-link agglomerative clustering'). No title word is reused — the title is 'cluster.ts — claim grouping by embedding similarity'.

single identifier token (medoidOf); appears in area-embedding-clustering's body and one of its claims, nowhere else. Mirrors probes.json's 'rrfFuse' probe — the shape where the semantic arm has nothing to embed and only the keyword arm can carry the hit.

the Ollama default base URL, stated only in area-embedding-providers' body ('Default baseUrl: http://localhost:11434'). A punctuated non-word token — the class the FTS analyzer splits, not a natural-language phrase.

constant name asserted as a claim on all three notes (3045358a1e63, the 0.65 line in embedding-config-parameters' body, d337763ee21a on arch-overview). Three legitimate answers, so top-3 is a real bar here rather than a formality.
the HTTP call the only shipping backend makes; in area-embedding-providers' body and in arch-overview's claim e787712f05f2. Neither title contains 'api' or 'embed' as a standalone token.

search.q: what happens to search when nothing is configured to encode text
search.why: the keyword-only fallback, asserted on all three: area-embedding-interface's summary ('when absent, memory retrieval degrades to keyword-only') and claim 5dba4e7acec9, arch-overview's 'Embeddings optional: keyword-only fallback when no embedder configured', area-embedding-providers' "'' disables semantic search (keyword-only)".

search.q: why can OpenAI not be used for this
search.why: area-embedding-providers' claim 0072362daa4c ('provider-openai and provider-anthropic have ModelProvider but no EmbeddingProvider implementation'); arch-overview's summary names Ollama as the provider. 'OpenAI' is a body/claim term, not a title term.
the command all three name as the way to re-embed after a model change ('Rebuild via `orc memory rebuild` re-embeds everything', 'Model change requires `orc memory rebuild`', 'Rebuild-safe').

search.q: which document did this run produce
search.why: aimed at the densest part of this corpus: the two outcome notes are near-restatements of each other and step-produce-map is the episodic note that made the file. All three genuinely answer (embedding-interfaces-map.md), so all three are listed rather than picking a favourite — a probe that named one would be grading tie-break luck.

search.q: how does the code notice someone swapped the model out
search.why: model-change detection stated as a question; the notes call it a DIMENSION MISMATCH — 'cosine() throws on dimension mismatch' (arch-overview, claim 3efdda0d78a1) and claim ddd529f6d9c4 on area-embedding-clustering. Zero vocabulary overlap with either note's title or summary.

search.q: what stops a huge file from being sent to the encoder
search.why: the 8000-character input cap, without the words 'chars', 'limit' or the constant name: claim 825bc552b28a (embedding-config-parameters), a033810cfa0f (area-embedding-storage), and area-embedding-interface's 'sliced to 8000 chars'.

search.q: can retrieval still answer if the vector backend is down
search.why: best-effort degradation, phrased as an operator would: arch-overview's 'Best-effort: embed failures log warning, write/search continues' and area-embedding-interface's 'May reject on backend failure; callers catch and fall back to keyword'. Distinct from the 'nothing configured' probe above — that is absence, this is failure.

search.q: the number that decides whether two statements belong to the same group
search.why: the reader remembers there is a cutoff but not that it is called MEMORY_CLUSTER_THRESHOLD or that its value is 0.65. Same three notes as the identifier probe above, which makes the pair a direct identifier-vs-description comparison on one fact.

search.q: the one function every backend has to implement
search.why: describes embed(texts) without naming it, the interface, or 'provider' — claim 4747692258b1 and arch-overview's data-flow line are the answers.

search.q: how does a note written today become findable by meaning tomorrow
search.why: the write-to-retrieve path spans two notes: the interface note owns embed()/embedWritten, the storage note owns the column and the cosine query. arch-overview is the only note that states the whole flow, so a single-note answer is necessarily partial.
